name: Data Centers and Digital Infrastructure
summary: Hyperscale build-to-suit and leased campuses, AI/GPU campuses, powered land and shell development, colocation/retail and edge facilities, plus the SPV/JV financing that now carries much of hyperscaler capex off balance sheet. Three distinct risk products share the label: powered land is option value until power is executed; a build-to-suit campus is a long lease whose credit is whoever actually owes the rent (hyperscaler parent vs SPV/JV); colocation is an operating business valued on EBITDA. Power is the binding constraint: a data center builds in 18 to 24 months while grid connection typically takes 3 to 7 years. The diligence spine is executed power by MW and date (electric service agreement, not a will-serve letter), firm service or curtailment the lease tolerates with BYOC assets in the security package, a lease guaranteed by the investment-grade parent for longer than the debt, delivery dates later than transformer delivery and energization, large-load tariff/ratepayer/moratorium risk, water seniority, and obsolescence (density and cooling). Uses energy-infrastructure.json for the behind-the-meter contract suite, DSCR tables and equipment checks.
one_check: Executed power by MW and date, firm or with curtailment the lease tolerates, matched to a lease the hyperscaler PARENT guarantees for longer than the debt; power without a lease is a development bet, a lease without delivered power is a walk right.

subtypes.name: Hyperscale build-to-suit / leased campus
subtypes.description: Long lease to an investment-grade hyperscaler; collateral is the lease and its guaranty; binding risks are who the tenant really is (parent vs SPV/JV), termination and contraction rights, and delivery-date LDs and walk rights. Includes SPV/JV off-balance-sheet structures (e.g., Intel-Apollo ~$11B JV).

subtypes.name: Colocation / retail / wholesale multi-tenant
subtypes.description: An operating business valued on EBITDA; binding risks are churn, pricing, power pass-through and ratepayer exposure (colocation centers raised consumer costs in the HBS study).

subtypes.name: Powered land, shell and development
subtypes.description: Entitlements, interconnection position and power; option value until power is executed; binding risks are power deliverability, energization date and permits.

subtypes.name: AI / GPU campus (high-density, often with on-site power)
subtypes.description: High-density (liquid-cooled) campuses for AI training/inference, often multi-GW and paired with behind-the-meter generation; adds obsolescence and compute-economics risk (DeepSeek) and curtailment/BYOC questions. The bible has no AI-specific benchmarks beyond the general data-center and power material.

subtypes.name: Edge / small distributed facilities
subtypes.description: Smaller distributed sites; diligence follows the colocation operating-asset checks (uptime, churn, power pass-through, fiber). The bible has no edge-specific material: thin coverage.

intake_questions.question: Which product is this: powered land/development, hyperscale build-to-suit or leased campus, AI/GPU campus, colocation, or edge?
intake_questions.why: Three distinct risk products share the label; underwrite the one you are offered (6A.1).

intake_questions.question: Who signs the lease: the hyperscaler parent, an SPV/JV, or a colocation tenant? Is there a parent guaranty?
intake_questions.why: The credit is whoever actually owes the rent (6A.1, 6A.6).

intake_questions.question: What is the power status by MW and date: queue/will-serve letter, facilities study, executed electric service agreement, or energized? Firm or curtailable?
intake_questions.why: Power is the binding constraint; a will-serve letter is not an ESA (6A.3).

intake_questions.question: Which utility and RTO serve the site (PJM, ERCOT, other), and which large-load tariff applies?
intake_questions.why: PJM 2026 proposals, ERCOT curtailment and tariff/rate-case risk differ by market (6A.3).

intake_questions.question: Is there behind-the-meter or bring-your-own generation? If so, fuel, air permit and equipment status?
What share of the demand case is signed leases, LOIs and forecast, in MW by year?
What is the water source and cooling design (air vs liquid), and is the site in a Colorado River-dependent market?
Is the financing at the asset, an SPV/JV, or corporate level, and what is the debt tenor against lease term?
intake_questions.why: Off-balance-sheet financing shifts the credit question to who owes the rent (6A.1).

requests.request: Provide the executed lease(s) (or, for colocation/edge, the customer contract schedule), not LOIs, with tenant entity named.
requests.format: Executed leases with all amendments; for operating assets, MSA/order-form schedule.
requests.why: Tenant LOI presented as a lease.
requests.pass: Executed lease(s) covering the MW in the sizing case.
requests.fail: LOI, MOU or term sheet only.

requests.request: Provide the executed electric service agreement or large-load interconnection agreement with the utility (not a will-serve letter).
requests.why: A will-serve letter presented as an ESA; 'up to X GW' with no executed agreement.
requests.pass: Executed agreement covering contracted MW with load ramp schedule.
requests.fail: Will-serve letter, queue position or 'up to X GW' marketing.

requests.request: Provide a schedule of MW contracted versus MW deliverable by date (energization schedule by MW).
requests.format: Table tied to the ESA load-ramp schedule and leases.
requests.why: Power arrives after the lease requires it.
requests.pass: Deliverable MW meets or precedes lease delivery MW at every date.
requests.fail: Gap between leased and deliverable MW.

requests.request: State what share of the demand case is signed leases, LOIs and forecast, in MW by year.
requests.format: Sponsor table reconciled to executed leases.
requests.why: A demand case that is a national forecast (DOE/LBNL 2028 range 325-580 TWh is the demand risk).
requests.pass: Sizing case uses signed leases only.
requests.fail: Forecast or LOI MW in sizing case.

requests.request: Provide site control and zoning evidence confirming data-center use is permitted by right.
requests.format: Deed/ground lease; zoning letter or ordinance extract.
requests.pass: Site controlled; DC use by right or entitled.
requests.fail: Requires discretionary approval not yet obtained.

requests.request: Confirm whether the site's power is firm or curtailable/non-firm, in writing from the utility.
requests.why: 'Secured power' that is non-firm or curtailable.
requests.pass: Firm service, or non-firm with written terms the lease tolerates.

requests.request: Provide the structure chart showing the SPV/JV, financing entities, and who owes rent and debt.
requests.why: Off-balance-sheet structures obscure who owes the rent.

requests.request: Provide the live financial model with lease cash flows, debt sizing, and DSCR mapped to S&P Table 8 logic (OPBA).
requests.why: Speculative or colocation assets sized like an IG lease.
requests.pass: IG long lease with no merchant tail: minimum DSCR within 1.10x-1.40x (OPBA 1-4); speculative/colocation sized with far more coverage per higher OPBA.
requests.fail: Colocation or spec sized at IG-lease coverage.
requests.verify: Rating adviser view on OPBA mapping.

requests.request: Provide the lease term versus debt tenor schedule including first termination/contraction option dates.
requests.pass: Debt amortizes within the firm lease term (to first termination option) or a re-lease case supports the balloon.
requests.fail: Debt tenor beyond first termination option without re-lease case.

requests.request: Provide the rate sensitivity at +200 bp on debt and discount rate.
Provide a re-lease / tenant-exit case: rent, downtime, re-leasing party and residual value if the tenant leaves at the first termination option.
requests.why: Compute economics fall (cheaper models, DeepSeek) and tenant walks.
requests.pass: Case shown; debt survives or is amortized before option.

requests.request: Provide a delivery-delay case: impact of a six-month late delivery on rent commencement, LDs payable and tenant walk rights.
requests.why: Tenant walk right on late delivery.
requests.pass: Liquidity covers LDs; walk-right date beyond realistic delivery with buffer.
requests.fail: Walk right reachable in a six-month delay.

requests.request: For colocation/edge, provide EBITDA-based valuation and leverage, with churn and renewal-spread assumptions.
requests.why: Operating business valued as a lease.
requests.pass: Leverage consistent with operating-company EBITDA multiples; churn assumptions tie to history.

requests.request: For powered land, provide valuation that treats queue position or will-serve letters as option value only.
requests.pass: No value ascribed to un-executed power beyond option value.

requests.request: Provide the energization-date stress against debt-service covenants.
requests.pass: Covenants survive 12- and 24-month delay or LDs/funding cover.

requests.request: Provide incremental transmission and capacity cost allocation: who pays and where it sits in the lease.
requests.why: Unallocated upgrade/capacity costs (PJM capacity costs ~$40B/3 years).
requests.pass: Costs allocated to tenant or priced in.

requests.request: Provide the parent guaranty: guarantor entity, scope, caps and release triggers.
requests.why: Lease signed by an SPV with no parent guaranty.
requests.pass: IG parent guarantees full rent and obligations for at least debt tenor; no release triggers before maturity.
requests.fail: No guaranty, capped guaranty, or release triggers.

requests.request: Provide a lease abstract covering early termination and contraction rights, assignment rights, rent escalators, delivery-date LDs, tenant walk rights and power pass-through.
requests.format: Counsel abstract tied to clause references.
requests.pass: No convenience termination or contraction before debt maturity, or debt sized to the option.
requests.fail: Termination rights inside debt tenor unaddressed.

requests.request: Provide the lease clause stating whether the lease tolerates curtailment, or confirm BYOC assets are in the security package.
requests.pass: Lease tolerates curtailment hours in the study, or BYOC assets pledged.

requests.request: Provide tenant/guarantor credit evidence: ratings and latest audited financials.
Provide tenant estoppel certificates.
Provide the utility facilities study, upgrade cost allocation and evidence of security posted.
requests.pass: Upgrades quantified, funded and security posted.

requests.request: Provide the energization date commitment with LDs in the ESA.
requests.pass: Energization date stated with LDs or remedy.

requests.request: For any non-firm/flexible connection, provide the utility's written flexible/non-firm service terms (hours and MW curtailable, notice, compensation).
requests.why: 'Fast-track' interconnection with no written flexible terms.

requests.request: Provide the site-specific hourly curtailment study (hours per year, MW curtailed, which hours, all 8,760 hours).
requests.why: ZERO Lab result cited as proof for this site.
requests.pass: Site-specific study; on-site generation/storage sized to cover the curtailment window.
requests.fail: Study absent or only ZERO Lab generic results cited.

requests.request: Provide backup/BYOC generation details: capacity, fuel, hours, and backup-generation air permit.
requests.why: Curtailment forces a switch to diesel without permit.
requests.pass: Backup sized for study hours and permitted.

requests.request: For behind-the-meter generation, provide the EPC, LTSA, fuel supply and air permit (apply the energy-infrastructure power-island checklist).
requests.why: Behind-the-meter gas plan with no air permit.
requests.pass: Full contract suite executed; LTSA availability 95%-98%.

requests.request: Provide the applicable large-load tariff and cost-allocation rules.
Provide a list of pending rate cases for the serving utility and their expected impact.
Provide local and state moratorium history and current proposals affecting data centers.
For PJM sites, provide analysis of the PJM January 2026 proposals (BYOG for firm service, connect-and-manage curtailable service, new-supply backstop auction) and FERC status.
requests.format: Counsel memo citing the PJM Board letter and FERC filings.
requests.pass: Impact quantified against final or filed terms.
requests.fail: Reliance on proposals without status check.
requests.verify: Read the PJM Board letter and FERC filings.

requests.request: State whether the site can reuse a brownfield interconnection (surplus interconnection service or retiring-unit replacement).
Provide power pass-through mechanics and percentage.
Provide the development agreement and GMP with contingency and the contractor's data-center track record.
requests.pass: GMP executed; contingency adequate per IE; contractor has comparable DC completions.

requests.request: Provide long-lead equipment purchase orders (transformers, switchgear, generators, chillers) with delivery dates, deposits and serial numbers.
requests.why: Reservation is not an order; speculative orders.
requests.pass: Firm POs; delivery before need date.

requests.request: Provide a schedule showing the delivery date is later than the transformer delivery date and later than energization.
requests.why: Delivery date earlier than transformer delivery.

requests.request: Provide the commissioning plan (Level 1 to 5).
requests.pass: Full L1-L5 plan with owner and schedule.

requests.request: Provide FAT, serial numbers and load-bank certificates for generators.
Provide an engineer's report on rack density supported, cooling (air vs liquid) and retrofit cost.
requests.pass: Density and cooling match tenant requirements; retrofit cost quantified and in re-lease case.

requests.request: Provide SLAs and uptime commitments with credits paid history.
Provide uptime/outage incident history.
Provide PUE trend.
requests.pass: Stable or improving trend (no primary benchmark; GAP).

requests.request: Provide churn and renewal spreads by customer.
Provide fiber and carrier agreements demonstrating route diversity.
Provide water rights/permits, source priority and cooling design.
requests.why: Water curtailed (Colorado River 16.5M af allocated vs ~12.5M flow).
requests.fail: Junior water in a Colorado River-dependent market.

requests.request: Provide property tax abatement agreements and clawback conditions.
Provide bound insurance quotes for the hold.
requests.pass: Bound for the hold; 2x premium stress passes.

requests.request: Provide the development budget with contingency and sources and uses.
For SPV/JV financings, provide the JV agreement, sponsor commitments and recourse to the hyperscaler.
requests.why: JV terminable lease with no recourse.

requests.request: Provide a memo on whether the tenant is hyperscaler-owned use or colocation and the resulting ratepayer exposure.
Commission a utility/interconnection consultant review: facilities study, firm vs non-firm terms, hourly curtailment study, upgrade allocation.
requests.pass: Consultant confirms MW by date and curtailment exposure.

requests.request: Commission an independent engineer: construction budget, schedule versus equipment and energization, density and cooling retrofit cost.
Commission a power-island IE for behind-the-meter generation (technology, availability, heat rate, air permit).
Commission lease counsel review: guaranty, termination, contraction, delivery LDs, curtailment tolerance.
Commission regulatory counsel on large-load tariff, rate cases and moratorium risk.
Commission water-rights counsel on source, seniority and curtailment.
Commission an insurance advisor to confirm bindable quotes for the hold.
Commission an equipment inspector for FAT, serial numbers and load-bank certificates.
Commission a quality-of-earnings review for operating assets.
Deliver executed parent guaranty and tenant estoppel/SNDA at closing.
Confirm ESA in force, security posted and energization schedule current at closing.
Provide bound insurance certificates naming lenders.
Provide monthly construction and equipment delivery reports against energization and lease delivery dates.
Provide curtailment event logs (hours, MW, backup dispatched).
Provide quarterly PUE, uptime, churn and renewal data.
Provide quarterly updates on tariff, rate case, moratorium and RTO rule changes.
Provide tenant/guarantor credit updates and DSCR compliance.

kill_tests.test: Power evidenced only by a will-serve letter, queue position or 'up to X GW' with no executed electric service agreement (except powered land valued as option only).
Lease signed by an SPV/JV with no parent guaranty, financed as if the parent owed the rent.
Tenant LOI presented as a lease in the sizing case.
Lease delivery date earlier than transformer delivery or energization, with a walk right reachable.
Non-firm power marketed as firm with no curtailment study and no lease tolerance or BYOC security.
Behind-the-meter gas plan with no air permit.

red_flags.flag: 'Up to X GW' of power with no executed agreement.
red_flags.check: Executed ESA by MW and date.

red_flags.flag: Lease signed by an SPV with no parent guaranty.
Tenant LOI presented as a lease.
Behind-the-meter gas plan with no air permit.
Delivery date earlier than the transformer delivery date.
'Secured power' that is non-firm or curtailable.
A 'fast-track' interconnection with no written flexible terms and no curtailment study.
The ZERO Lab two-year result cited as proof for this site (six PJM sites, one utility, Google-funded, disputed).
A will-serve letter presented as an electric service agreement.
A demand case that is a national forecast, not signed leases.
A colocation business with no view on its utility's rate case or large-load tariff.
No water source or seniority in a Colorado River-dependent market.
Queue position or will-serve letters given more than option value in a powered-land valuation.
Speculative equipment reservations presented as firm orders.
Retrospective 'load growth lowers rates' studies used to dismiss ratepayer risk.

metrics.metric: Minimum DSCR, IG long lease, no merchant tail (S&P OPBA 1-4 mapping, judgment)
metrics.source: S&P General PF Methodology 2022 Table 8 (mapping is judgment; ask rating adviser)

metrics.acceptable: Higher OPBA: far more coverage (S&P OPBA 5-8: 1.30x-2.50x; 9-10: 2.50x-5.00x)
Build-to-suit tracks tenant credit and lease term; colocation trades on EBITDA like an operating company

metrics.metric: Data-center build time vs grid connection
metrics.acceptable: Build 18-24 months; grid 3-7 years typical
8-12 years (Goldman via gi-advisors, WEAK) | 3-7 years (ZERO Lab 2025) | >5, 7+ years (Kleinman 2025, WEAK) | 61-month median request-to-COD (LBNL 2026)

metrics.metric: Flexible connection (ZERO Lab): time to full operation
metrics.acceptable: ~2 years with flexible connection + BYOC, 3-5 years faster; grid power >99% of hours; on-site dispatch 40-70 h/yr; transmission curtailment 7-35 h/yr in 4-16 h events, peak up to 281 MW; generation shortfalls ~32 additional h/yr. Six 500 MW sites in one PJM utility only.
metrics.source: Brancucci, Cutler, Jenkins, ZERO Lab Dec 2025 (Google-funded and reviewed)

metrics.metric: Firm-only vs flexible system cost per GW (ZERO Lab)
metrics.acceptable: Firm-only adds ~$764M/yr system supply cost per GW (2.17 GW nameplate); 20% conditional-firm avoids 273 MW ($78M); BYOC internalizes $326M; energy payments $329M; net DC covers ~$733M/GW
~176 TWh, ~4.4% of U.S. electricity
metrics.source: DOE/LBNL 2024 Data Center Energy Usage Report

metrics.acceptable: 325-580 TWh, ~6.7%-12% (the width IS the demand risk)
Up to 15% (secondhand; different horizon from DOE/LBNL 2028)

metrics.metric: Utility peak demand growth from DCs
metrics.acceptable: +20% to 40%+ over a decade (Midwest, Southeast, Southwest, Texas)
33 GW by 2031 (36% of 91 GW peak); 175 GW peak by 2032 floated (forecasts, not contracts)
~6.5 GW/yr through 2030
~460 TWh, ~2% of global
Right-skewed: most Texas campuses < 0.5 GW, a few multi-GW
~$116B (2022) to nearly $200B (2024); 2025 plans ~$80B MSFT, $65B Meta, $75B Alphabet, $100B Amazon; worldwide DC capex +51% to ~$455B (2024)
385 DCs/42 utilities 2020-2025: ~16% of industrial and 4% of residential price increases (~$5.40/MWh industrial, $1.70/MWh residential); colocation raised consumer costs, hyperscaler-owned did not
~$40B over three years, ~half DCs (IMM) | NRDC $47B
1922 Compact 16.5M af/yr vs ~12.5M af/yr 2000-2023 flows

metrics.metric: LTSA availability for BTM power island

metrics.acceptable: +200 bp on debt and discount rate
GAP: Uptime Institute survey not retrieved; no acceptable threshold set
GAP: no primary source retrieved

third_party_reports.report: Utility/interconnection review (facilities study, firm vs non-firm, hourly curtailment study, upgrade allocation)
Independent engineer report (budget, schedule vs equipment and energization, density, cooling retrofit cost)
Power-island IE report (technology, availability, heat rate, air permit)
Lease review (guaranty, termination, contraction, delivery LDs, curtailment tolerance)
Regulatory memo (large-load tariff, rate cases, moratorium)

third_party_reports.required_when: Always; mandatory in arid/Colorado River markets

third_party_reports.report: Equipment inspection (FAT, serial numbers, load-bank certificates)

hard_questions.question: Show the executed utility agreement and the energization schedule by MW.
hard_questions.good_answer: Executed ESA with load-ramp table matching lease delivery MW.

hard_questions.question: Who guarantees the lease?
hard_questions.good_answer: The rated hyperscaler parent, full scope, no release before debt maturity.

hard_questions.question: What happens if delivery is six months late?
hard_questions.good_answer: Clause-referenced answer: LDs payable funded by contingency, walk right not reachable.

hard_questions.question: What density does the building support, and what does a liquid-cooling retrofit cost?
hard_questions.good_answer: Engineer's figure per MW and a retrofit cost included in the re-lease case.

hard_questions.question: Which equipment is on firm order with serial numbers?
hard_questions.good_answer: PO list with serials and delivery dates before need dates.

hard_questions.question: Is your interconnection firm or flexible? How many hours per year can the utility curtail you, and what carries the load during those hours?
hard_questions.good_answer: Written terms, site-specific hourly study, permitted BYOC sized to the hours.

hard_questions.question: Who pays for network upgrades and incremental capacity costs, and is that in the lease?
Which large-load tariff applies, what rate cases are pending, and has the county or state considered a moratorium?
hard_questions.good_answer: Named tariff, docket list and moratorium history with modelled impact.

hard_questions.question: If the tenant leaves at the first termination option, who re-leases it, at what rent, and what does the debt look like?
hard_questions.good_answer: A re-lease case with downtime and rent haircut, debt amortized or refinanceable.

hard_questions.question: What is your water source and its priority?
hard_questions.good_answer: Senior right or contract with priority date, or dry/closed-loop cooling.

hard_questions.question: What share of the demand case is signed leases, LOIs and forecast, by MW and year?
hard_questions.good_answer: Table with sizing on signed leases only.

hard_questions.question: What happens to the asset if compute demand per dollar falls (cheaper models)?

failure_cases.case: Powered-land story without power (failure mode; no named case sourced, GAP)
failure_cases.what_happened: Sites marketed on queue positions or will-serve letters.
failure_cases.check: Executed utility agreement and energization schedule; queue/will-serve as option value only.

failure_cases.case: Tenant walk right on late delivery (failure mode)
failure_cases.what_happened: Tenant terminates when building is late.
failure_cases.check: Read delivery-date and termination clauses against realistic equipment and energization timeline.

failure_cases.case: SPV tenant, not the hyperscaler parent (failure mode)
failure_cases.what_happened: Rent owed by a terminable SPV/JV.

failure_cases.case: Stranded asset on design obsolescence (failure mode)
failure_cases.check: Engineer's report on density and retrofit cost.

failure_cases.what_happened: ~13 GW of reservations cancelled, ~$3.7B reported loss.

failure_cases.case: Curtailable service sold as firm (PJM 2026 proposals)
failure_cases.what_happened: Connect-and-manage service may force a switch to diesel backup.
failure_cases.check: Written firm/non-firm terms; hourly curtailment study; BYOC in security package.

failure_cases.what_happened: 20% residential bill increase in parts of NJ became a governor's-race issue.
failure_cases.check: Large-load tariff, cost allocation, rate cases, moratorium history.

failure_cases.case: Demand that never shows up (failure mode)
failure_cases.what_happened: Stranded grid build-out (Kleinman, WEAK); DOE/LBNL 2028 range 325-580 TWh.
Falling model costs flagged as risk to DC economics.
failure_cases.check: Re-lease case; residual value on tenant exit.

failure_cases.what_happened: Others build to serve the same load, lowering prices.
~20% of DC pipeline faces power/grid delays (vendor, WEAK).
failure_cases.check: Executed agreement with funded upgrades, milestones, energization stressed against covenants.
